F21.quote: Kummel provides the following information on dating the Apocalypse of John ( Introduction to the New Testament , pp. 466-8):
F21.claim: the page's dating information is quoted from Kümmel's Introduction to the New Testament, pp. 466-8
F21.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F22.quote: According to the oldest tradition [in Iren., Adv. Haer. 5.30.3] Rev was written toward the end of the reign of Domitian (81-96).
F22.claim: the oldest tradition (Irenaeus, Adv. Haer. 5.30.3) places Revelation toward the end of Domitian's reign (81-96)
F22.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F23.quote: The book's own testimony indicates that it originated in the province of Asia in a time of severe oppression of Christians, which is most readily conceivable under Domitian.
F23.claim: the internal testimony: Asia, severe oppression, most readily conceivable under Domitian
F23.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F24.quote: Christianity has collided with the state and with the state religion, the Christ cult with the imperial cult.
F24.claim: the collision with the imperial cult
F24.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F25.quote: Prior to Domitian, the state religion did not direct itself against the Christians. Nero's mad acts in Rome against the Christians had nothing to do with the imperial cult.
F25.claim: before Domitian the state religion did not act against Christians; Nero's acts had nothing to do with the imperial cult
F25.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F26.quote: the Antichrist, the "beast" (13:1 ff, etc.), does not bear the features of any specific ruler but rather those of the demonic form of Nero redivivus , which was still a popular expectation in that time.
F26.claim: the beast bears the features of Nero redivivus, not of a specific ruler
F26.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F27.quote: Also favoring the end of the first century as the time of origin of Rev is the fact that according to 2:8-11, the church of Smyrna has been persevering for a long time, while according to Polycarp (Phil 11:3), at the time of Paul it did not even exist; and 3:17 describes the community of Laodicea as rich, while this city had been almost completely destroyed by an earthquake in A.D. 60/61.
F27.claim: further grounds for the end of the first century: Smyrna's long perseverance (Polycarp, Phil 11:3) and Laodicea's wealth after the earthquake of 60/61
F27.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F28.quote: In all likelihood, therefore, Rev was in fact written toward the end of the reign of Domitian, i.e., ca. 90-95, in Asia Minor, in order to encourage Christian communities threatened by a destructive persecution to endure and to make them confident of the imminent victory of Christ over the powers of the Antichrist.
F28.claim: Kümmel's conclusion: in all likelihood written toward the end of Domitian's reign, ca. 90-95, in Asia Minor, to encourage persecuted communities
F28.lineage: the quoted introduction: Kümmel's case for the Domitianic date

F29.quote: Traditionally it has been claimed that he is the John, son of Zebedee, known to us from the gospel stories, but this is most unlikely. It has also been claimed that he is the "John" of the fourth gospel, but the difference in language and style alone makes this identification quite impossible.
F29.claim: Perrin (The New Testament: An Introduction, pp. 81-2): the seer is most unlikely the son of Zebedee and cannot be the 'John' of the fourth gospel
F29.lineage: the quoted introduction: Perrin on the seer and the letter form

F30.quote: This is unparalleled in apocalyptic writing and has to be due ultimately to the impact that Paul's letter writing made on the New Testament church. Paul's letters had become so important that the literary form was imitated even by an apocalyptic writer.
F30.claim: Perrin: the letters to seven churches are due to the impact of Paul's letter writing; the form was imitated by an apocalyptic writer
F30.lineage: the quoted introduction: Perrin on the seer and the letter form

F31.quote: It is a reminder that for all its surface strangeness, the book of Revelation is not to be separated from the rest of the New Testament.
F31.claim: Perrin: Revelation is not to be separated from the rest of the New Testament
F31.lineage: the quoted introduction: Perrin on the seer and the letter form
